title: Hard feasibility before Pareto ranking
summary: dev6 makes feasibility a separate authority layer. An infeasible candidate may remain search/evidence, but no objective advantage can buy its way into a Pareto front or promotion set.
authority: Executable ooRexx ML dev6 MLConstraints.cls and regressions are authoritative.
invariants: Hard constraints are gates, not objectives and not large penalty weights.
MLConstrainedEvaluatorAdapter evaluates constraints before expensive objective scoring and publishes no objective vector for an infeasible subject.
Infeasible candidates remain evidence; they may be ordered by violation count only as a search-recovery heuristic.
Only feasible candidates participate in Pareto dominance/front construction.
Only feasible Pareto points may enter MLConstrainedParetoRetentionSelector promotion output.
MLConstrainedParetoGeneticAlgorithm preserves transactional checkpoint, deterministic RNG, rollback/replay and final-bred-generation evaluation semantics.
procedure: Declare non-tradable requirements as MLHardConstraint objects and group them in MLConstraintSet.
Wrap the domain evaluator in MLConstrainedEvaluatorAdapter so infeasible inputs fail before scores().
Analyze with MLConstrainedParetoAnalyzer; inspect infeasible assessments separately from feasible fronts.
For GA search, use MLConstrainedParetoGeneticAlgorithm; never scalarize hard violations into the objective vector.

provenance.claim: Hard constraints, constrained evaluation, constrained Pareto analysis/retention and constrained Pareto GA implementation.
Regression proves an objectively superior hard-constraint violator is retained as evidence but excluded from frontier and promotion.
Regression proves infeasible subjects are rejected before expensive scoring and receive no objective vector.
Regression proves constrained Pareto rollback/replay reproduces offspring and RNG state.
